To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a method for direct reconstruction of velocity fields at specified scale from particle tracks in a flow, with no need for interpolation or grid generation, and that the method eliminates the effects of outlier particles and reduces compressibility of the velocity fields.
the method is able to reconstruct velocity fields from measurements with a high degree of fidelity and to produce scale-local properties directly.

a direct, scale-specific reconstruction of velocity fields is possible using observational data from particles in a flow; the reconstruction is based on a least squares projection of the data onto a set of modes with known length scale, and is evaluated at particle locations without interpolation onto an artificial grid; the method is useful for identifying scale-to-scale transfer, for eliminating outlier particles automatically, and for evaluating the spatial effects of the open boundaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of two-dimensional velocity fields from measurements made on a set of tracer particles, without the need to interpolate or smooth the data.
the development of methods to analyze data obtained from tracer particles in fluid flows, and with the application of these methods to the study of oceanic flows and other geophysical flows.

the development of a new methodology to reconstruct the two-dimensional velocity field in a region from a finite set of particle tracks, and to evaluate the effects of scale and open boundaries on that field.
